name: Cement Grey
lede: Cement Grey is a greenish grey that three separate systems named within a few decades of each other: Ridgway's 1912 plates, the 1927 RAL industrial standard, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary.

sections.title: Three systems, one grey
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature plates a version of it at plate LII, hue 35''''', and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately dates a plate to the same year, column C, chip 2 [1]. The German RAL industrial color standard also lists a near-identical grey, RAL 7033, from 1927, independently of either color dictionary [1]. The ISCC-NBS committee's 1955 match places the hex #818979 among the "greenish gray" names, 5.0 units away [1]. No Munsell renotation is recorded for this entry, unusually for a Ridgway-sourced color [1].

Its closest library neighbors are [[deep-olive-grey|Deep Olive-Grey]], about 3.3 units away, and [[concrete-grey|Concrete Grey]], a near-twin at 3.7 units and an obvious partner in meaning, since cement and concrete are the same building material [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of Cement Grey covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 1,077 of 23,781 paintings, about 4.5 per cent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1940s, after the RAL industrial standard existed, though the archive cannot show whether that is cause or coincidence [2]. Berthe Morisot carries it nearly nine times the archive average, more than any other painter [2]. Its earliest appearance is a *Mahamayuri Vidyaraja* dated to around 916 [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors [2].

disambiguation.gloss: Concrete Grey is a near-identical grey named for the related building material, 3.7 units away
